# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives the mapping: in the listed light order (green, red, yellow), the required wire-cut colors are (red, yellow, green), i.e. positions 2, 3, 1. I’m encoding those positions with one, two, and three fingers so Deaf can decode the mapping and relay it by voice to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤟", "☝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see colours or markings. Tell me the manual's exact rule and ask Deaf to report every visible detail, including which wire position is safe. Relay Deaf's answer to me next round.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb reads display 0. Light is green. Wires in order are yellow, green, red. I saw your gestures: victory hand, I-love-you hand, raised index finger. Please clarify their meaning through the available channel.

The current light is green, so the manual requires cutting the red wire. Since the wires are ordered yellow, green, red, the safe choice is wire position 3. Deaf can see the bomb and can tell Blind this by voice; I signal the third position using the established finger-count code.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0, green light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Please state the manual's exact rule in words and identify the safe wire position.
Deaf says to Mute: I received 🤟. Please encode its manual meaning unambiguously in gestures, and I will relay it aloud to Blind.

The manual’s rule is already encoded by the established finger-count convention: for lights in the manual’s order green, red, yellow, the required wire positions are 2, 3, 1. Repeating the complete sequence removes ambiguity, and Deaf can state the rule aloud to Blind. For the present green light, this identifies wire 2—not wire 3—so I correct the earlier mistaken signal.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤟", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your gesture does not reach me as a readable message. Speak the manual rule in words, including the safe wire position for display 0, green light, and yellow-green-red wires.

I cannot speak to Blind. I can communicate through Deaf, who can hear and relay the information. The exact rule is green light → red wire, red light → yellow wire, yellow light → green wire. With wires yellow, green, red, the green-light instruction means position 3. I will send the complete mapping and repeat position 3 to Deaf using our established number gestures.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤟", "☝", "🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received the encoded numbers 2, 3, 1 through Deaf. State in words exactly what they mean for this bomb and which single wire position I should cut.

I cannot speak, and Blind cannot read my gestures. Deaf must relay the rule aloud. The sequence 2, 3, 1 means: green light → wire position 2 in the manual’s abstract mapping, red → 3, yellow → 1; however, for this bomb the visible wires are yellow, green, red, so green light requires the red wire at position 3. I will reinforce the complete mapping and the immediate choice to Deaf.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤟", "☝", "🤟"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Do not send the full code. Signal exactly one gesture for the safe wire position: victory means wire 2, I-love-you means wire 3, raised index means wire 1.

The green light requires the red wire. Since Deaf reported the wire order as yellow, green, red, the safe wire is position 3. Using the specified code, I send exactly one I-love-you gesture for wire 3.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```
